headline: Content pipeline rebuild cuts manual work 50%, fixes timezone publishing drift
summary: A developer overhauled their content pipeline, automating AI-generated drafts into a structured staging area. This cut manual copy-paste work by 50% and resolved critical timezone-related publishing errors across platforms.
details: A developer successfully rebuilt their content pipeline, cutting manual copy-paste work in half and fixing persistent timezone-related publishing errors. The previous setup involved manually distributing AI-generated drafts from a raw content directory to platforms like Substack, Medium, and Dev.to.

The core problem was a manual bottleneck in content distribution, compounded by GitHub Actions cron jobs hardcoded to UTC. This led to inconsistent publishing times and a significant amount of daily manual effort to format and publish content across multiple platforms.

Initial attempts to automate with a flat directory and a single cron job failed due to API rate limits, unescaped HTML issues, and frequently changing JSON structures for platform APIs. A monolithic workflow also meant that a single platform failure would halt the entire publishing process.

The new implementation shifted to a staging-first architecture, routing content to Craft Docs via a `craft_publisher.py` script. Craft Docs now serves as an 'inbox' for daily drafts, with published content automatically archived, providing a crucial manual review layer without breaking automation.

The data model was updated to support the new platform, requiring a rewrite of the publisher script into a platform-agnostic document creator. API calls were isolated into a separate function to ensure workflows fail fast with clear errors if external APIs are down.

The monolithic GitHub Actions workflow was split into separate, platform-specific workflows for Medium, Email, Bluesky, and Dev.to. Crucially, explicit timezone comments were added to cron triggers, and timezone/brand settings were baked into the pipeline configuration, ensuring deterministic publishing schedules.

headline: Save $1,430 on Legion Tower 7i Gen 10 RTX 5080 gaming PC with Core Ultra 7 265K
summary: Lenovo's high-end gaming rig, featuring an RTX 5080 and Core Ultra 7 265K, is now available for $2,899.99, a 33% discount.
details: You can save up to $1,430 on the Lenovo Legion Tower 7i Gen 10 gaming PC, which is currently priced at $2,899.99. This represents a 33% discount, making a prebuilt system a cost-effective alternative to building your own.

The Legion Tower 7i Gen 10 is equipped with a Core Ultra 7 265K processor, featuring 20 cores and a boost clock speed of up to 5.5 GHz. This CPU is paired with a high-end GeForce RTX 5080, providing ample power to run the latest AAA games at 4K resolution.

The system comes with 32GB (2x16GB) of DDR5-5600 memory, ensuring smooth multitasking and gaming performance. For storage, it includes a 2TB PCIe 4.0 SSD, offering fast load times and generous space for games and applications.

Cooling is handled by a 360mm AIO liquid cooler, capable of dissipating up to 250W, which is sufficient to keep the Core Ultra 7 265K cool during extended gaming sessions. Connectivity options include Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3 for high-speed internet and wireless peripherals.

Similar gaming systems with a Core Ultra 7 265K and GeForce RTX 5080 can cost up to $3,400, making this Lenovo deal highly competitive. Additionally, Lenovo includes a free three-month subscription to Xbox PC Game Pass with EA Play, offering access to over 100 titles.
